Standard: The AR system includes necessary mating equipment to facilitate engagement and disengagement procedures with targeted tanker/receiver AR subsystem without interference, binding or damage that would prevent AR operations. a. Boom Tanker. Tanker boom nozzle design includes an induction coil that meets dimensions and positioning of ATP-3.3.4.5, Annex B, Boom Nozzle Induction Coil Position figure, and Boom Nozzle Induction Coil Centering and Gap figure. b. Drogue tanker. The reception coupling has three equally spaced locking roller mechanisms. c. Receptacle receiver. Receptacle includes an induction coil that meets the dimension and positioning of ATP-3.3.4.5, Annex B, Receptacle Induction Coil Requirements figure and Receptacle Induction Coil Dimensions table. Receptacle is equipped with latches that conform to the dimensions and positioning of ATP-3.3.4.5, Latch Dimensions paragraph. Receptacle incorporates rollers that conform to the dimensional and positioning requirements of ATP-3.3.4.5, Receptacle Rollers figure and Receptacle Rollers table. Receptacle includes a contact sensor, designed to sense a contact when the receptacle sliding valve travels between 0.5 in and 0.75 in, that meets the dimensions and positioning of ATP-3.3.4.5, Receptacle Contact Sensor paragraph. d. Probe receiver. Probe nozzle incorporates two equally spaced sleeve latches. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Examination of drawings, specifications, and installed subsystem verifies boom nozzle mating equipment conforms to the dimension and positioning of the induction coil. b. Drogue Tanker. Examination of drawings, specifications, and installed subsystem verifies the reception coupling has three equally spaced locking roller mechanisms. c. Receptacle Receiver. Examination of drawings, specifications, and installed subsystem verifies receptacle mating equipment conforms to the dimension and positioning of the induction coil, latches, rollers, and contact sensor. d. Probe Receiver. Examination of drawings, specifications, and installed subsystem verifies probe nozzle has two equally spaced latches. Demonstration.
  (1) Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. 1. Demonstration in a laboratory environment verifies tanker boom nozzle induction coil alignment with targeted receiver(s) receptacle induction coil. 2. Ground demonstration verifies boom nozzle induction coil alignment with targeted receiver air vehicle(s) receptacle interface. b. Drogue Tanker. 1. Demonstration in a laboratory environment verifies probe engagement and disengagement with targeted tanker reception coupling without interference. 2. Ground demonstration verifies reception coupling engagement and disengagement with targeted receiver air vehicle(s) probe nozzle without interference. c. Receptacle Receiver. 1. Demonstration, with targeted tanker boom nozzle, in a laboratory environment, verifies signal coil alignment and operation, engagement and disengagement without interference, and contact sensor operation. 2. Air vehicle ground demonstration with targeted tanker boom nozzle verifies signal coil alignment and operation, engagement and disengagement without interference, and contact sensor operation. d. Probe Receiver. 1. Demonstration in a laboratory environment verifies probe engagement and disengagement with targeted tanker reception coupling without interference. 2. Air vehicle ground demonstration verifies probe nozzle engagement and disengagement with targeted tanker reception coupling without interference. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (1) Flight test: Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Flight testing with receptacle-equipped receivers verifies signal coil alignment and operation. Test points include worst-case combinations of tanker and receiver gross weights and CGs, at all extents of the boom disconnect envelope, minimum Mach, maximum Mach, minimum dynamic pressure and maximum dynamic pressure conditions, straight and level flight, in turns, and while tobogganing. b. Drogue Tanker. Flight testing verifies probe nozzle engagement and disengagement with tanker reception coupling without interference. Test points include wet and dry contacts, receiver closure rates of up to 10 ft/s, minimum Mach, maximum Mach, and minimum and maximum dynamic pressure conditions. c. Receptacle Receiver. Flight testing with boom-equipped tankers verifies signal coil alignment and operation, boom nozzle engagement and disengagement without interference, and contact sensor operation. Test points include worst-case combinations of tanker and receiver gross weights and CGs, at all extents of the boom disconnect envelope, wet and dry contacts, minimum Mach, maximum Mach, minimum dynamic pressure and maximum dynamic pressure conditions, straight and level flight, in turns, and while tobogganing. d. Probe Receiver. Flight testing with drogue-equipped tankers verifies probe nozzle engagement and disengagement without interference. Test points include wet and dry contacts, receiver closure rates of up to 10 ft/s, minimum Mach, maximum Mach, minimum dynamic pressure, and maximum dynamic pressure conditions.
